s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of headache and vision loss with sinus inflammation and orbital involvement
salient_findings: Vision loss in the right eye for 2 days
Opacification of all sinuses on the right with diffuse inflammation
Bony erosion of the medial orbital apex bone
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 70s
No history of chronic or allergic rhinosinusitis
Diagnosed with COVID-19 three weeks prior to presentation
Developed rhinorrhea and recovered from COVID-19
Worsening right-sided headache started 1 week after COVID-19 recovery
Right eye visual acuity limited to hand-motion detection
Severe pain on ocular motion
Sinus cultures positive for Streptococcus constellatus
Elevated Serum IgG4 level

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of headache and vision loss with sinus inflammation and orbital involvement
salient_findings: Vision loss in the right eye for 2 days
Opacification of all sinuses on the right with diffuse inflammation
Bony erosion of the medial orbital apex bone
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 70s
No history of chronic or allergic rhinosinusitis
Diagnosed with COVID-19 three weeks prior to presentation
Developed rhinorrhea and recovered from COVID-19
Worsening right-sided headache started 1 week after COVID-19 recovery
Right eye visual acuity limited to hand-motion detection
Severe pain on ocular motion
Sinus cultures positive for Streptococcus constellatus
Elevated Serum IgG4 level

raw.rationale: Elevated Serum IgG4 level and dense infiltrate of IgG-containing plasma cells, with most being IgG4 positive, are key evidence-based reasons for this diagnosis

rejected.label: Orbital Apex Syndrome
rejected.why: While the patient has symptoms consistent with Orbital Apex Syndrome, such as vision loss and severe pain on ocular motion, the specific findings of elevated IgG4 levels and IgG4-positive plasma cells point more strongly towards IgG4-related disease

rejected.label: Fungal Orbital Infection
rejected.why: There is no mention of fungal elements in the pathology or laboratory findings, making this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Cavernous Sinus Thrombosis
rejected.why: The imaging studies do not mention thrombosis in the cavernous sinus, and the clinical presentation does not strongly suggest this diagnosis

rejected.label: Granulomatosis with Polyangiitis
rejected.why: While this condition can cause similar symptoms, the specific IgG4-related findings and the absence of other characteristic features of Granulomatosis with Polyangiitis make it a less likely diagnosis
